reality_delta: Runtime validators were updated with new required fields and checks, which is a real code change. However, the accompanying test and fixture updates (e2e_trace.py, self-development-lifecycle-packet.json) suggest the gate was validated by making existing paths compliant rather than by demonstrating it blocks a non-compliant packet. The extraction artifact exists, but we cannot verify whether its behavioral questions were pre-defined drivers or post-hoc justifications.
main_concern: The new gate may be a schema-compliance check that has never been exercised against a failure. All evidence shows things passing; no evidence shows the gate catching a missing track, governance gap, or insufficient evidence. Without a demonstrated rejection, the implementation may be structurally real but functionally untested.
top_risks: Tests and fixtures were updated to include the new review_tracks fields, so 'all pass' only proves forward compatibility, not that the gate protects against under-reviewed work.
The behavioral questions in the extraction may have been written after implementation to satisfy the shard validator, rather than serving as pre-defined acceptance criteria.
The review_tracks check may verify presence and labels without evaluating depth or quality, making it a box-checking gate.
missing_evidence: A concrete example (historical or constructed) of a packet that the new gate rejects for missing tracks, governance, or evidence.
Proof that the behavioral questions were defined before extraction and implementation began.
Evidence that the gate differentiates between superficially-present tracks and substantively complete tracks.
minimum_fix: Run or document a falsification test: attempt to advance a medium-priority packet without review_tracks and confirm it is blocked. If the system cannot produce such a rejection, the gate is unproven. The extraction's behavioral questions should also be shown to pre-date the implementation commit.

anti_loop_signal.reason: The main AI has delivered code changes, not just documents. Good. Watch for the loop where every new gate is immediately followed by updating all fixtures and tests to comply, so the gate is never observed rejecting anything.

user_intent_alignment: Medium-High. The user asked for real implementation, and code was changed. But the user also asked for Prism assistance to ensure it was not record-only progress; without proof the gate catches failures, the implementation may be structurally real but functionally ceremonial.
